thread:
anna_support: FYI escalation from ACME — streaming responses over our hosted API intermittently cut off mid-stream when customer goes through their gRPC -> HTTP/1.1 gateway. They see partial outputs, then client reconnects and sometimes gets duplicate final chunks. Customer says issue started after they put an envoy/gw in front of the client. Ticket #5631.

anna_support: Repro steps they provided: curl to our /v1/stream endpoint with SSE (text/event-stream) works from their app directly, but via their gateway it truncates after ~3-5s. They included a small curl they used:

```
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=llama-2&prompt=hello"
```

anna_support: "-N" on curl to disable buffering; they said adding `--no-buffer` didn't help when going through gw. Also they see `RST_STREAM` on the gateway logs occasionally.

mike_eng: Thanks @anna_support — can you paste the gateway config? Common culprits: proxy buffering, chunked_transfer_encoding, TE: trailers, and keepalive/timeout mismatches between HTTP/2 upstream and HTTP/1.1 downstream.

anna_support: Added the gateway snippet they have: (redacted IPs)

```
# gateway snippet (they run a custom gRPC gateway that translates to http1)
server {
  proxy_pass http://upstream;
  proxy_buffering on; # default
  proxy_read_timeout 30s;
}
```

maya_net: That proxy_buffering on looks suspicious. If the gateway buffers until upstream completes or a buffer fills, streaming semantics break. For SSE we need passthrough chunking. If it sits in front as http2->http1, you want `proxy_buffering off` and `chunked_transfer_encoding on` or equivalent. Also ensure they forward trailers/TE headers.

simon_sre: We also saw RST_STREAM in their logs — could be the gateway closing the h2 stream if it thinks the backend is idle. Do we have logs from our edge during the timeframe? @deploy-bot can you correlate deploys/changes around 1799993940-1799994120?

deploy-bot: No recent deploys to api-hosting between 1799992000 and 1799994800.

mike_eng: Can we reproduce with a quick proxy that mimics their gateway? I can spin up an http2 -> http1 proxy locally using envoy or nginx. If we can reproduce, we should capture tcpdump and h2 frames to confirm RST/GOAWAY reasons.

anna_support: Customer provided a small capture from gateway showing repeated `write() returned 0` followed by `connection closed`. They also included their backend behavior: direct call to our API from inside their VPC (no gw) streams fine.

mike_eng: Repro attempt steps I used (local):
```
# start a simple envoy with http2 upstream and http1 downstream (rough sketch)
# client -> envoy (http1) -> envoy (http2) -> our api
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <localkey>" \ 
  "http://localhost:8080/proxy/v1/streams?prompt=ping"
```
I saw the same truncation when envoy had `max_stream_duration_ms` low and `http1/streaming` disabled.

mike_eng: Quick findings: when intermediary buffers and converts h2->h1, the last chunk sometimes gets coalesced and the gateway times out waiting for end-of-stream. If it tears down the h2 stream early, the client gets partial payload and may reconnect.

maya_net: Two actionable checks for customer: 1) ensure their gateway disables buffering for streaming routes, 2) set timeouts high enough and avoid `proxy_read_timeout` that matches token emission cadence. Also ensure they're passing `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` downstream and preserving `:status 200` and `content-type: text/event-stream`.

anna_support: I asked the customer to try a change: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 120s; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and to forward TE/trailer headers. They tried and reported improvement — fewer truncations but still an occasional disconnect.

simon_sre: If intermittent remains, let's look at keepalive and connection window sizes between their gateway and our edge. Window exhaustion can manifest as stalls then resets. @mike_eng can you add logging for window updates on our side for the session id in their logs?

mike_eng: Will add session-level h2 debug logs for that client key for 24h. Also asked customer for their gateway version; they run custom gRPC gateway v1.13 with default buffering.

anna_support: Also escalating potential billing edge-case to @lucy_billing — customer says some responses counted toward usage even though they consider them "failed streams" because output truncated mid-response. They want advice on credits.

lucy_billing: Happy to review. We typically bill on tokens emitted by the model. If the model emitted tokens and we delivered them to the gateway, that's usage. If we aborted server-side before emitting, not billed. If they have a policy dispute we can offer a one-off credit while the engineering team investigates. Please collect 3 example request ids and timestamps.

mike_eng: Follow-up: we pushed a temporary mitigation at the edge — allow longer idle time for client streams that contain `Accept: text/event-stream` and preserve streaming semantics even if the downstream signals a short read. This will be monitored and will not affect non-streaming endpoints.

anna_support: Customer tested again after toggling buffering off and our edge change — much better, two tests without truncation. They asked if we can recommend a long-term fix on their gateway.

mike_eng: Long-term: either 1) use a passthrough proxy that preserves http2 semantics (best), or 2) configure the gateway for true streaming: disable buffering, enable chunked transfer encoding, forward TE/trailer headers, increase read timeouts, and preserve connection keepalive. For Envoy/nginx specifics I suggested:
```
# nginx example
proxy_buffering off;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection ""; # avoid adding connection header
proxy_set_header TE "trailers";
proxy_read_timeout 120s;
```

mike_eng: For envoy, ensure `use_remote_address`, `http1_protocol_options->allow_chunked_length`, and `stream_idle_timeout` are configured to allow long-lived streams.

maya_net: We should also document this in devex notes for customers using gRPC gateways. Might prevent future escalations. @anna_support can you open a short KB article?

anna_support: Will create KB "SSE and streaming gotchas with HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 gateways" and include nginx/envoy examples + repro guidance + what to collect (tcpdump, RST_STREAM logs, request ids).

simon_sre: Marking as root cause: intermediary buffering + timeout mismatches during http2->http1 conversion leading to premature stream termination. Resolution: customer config changes + our edge idle extension. Keeping ticket open for 48h monitoring.

anna_support: Closing loop with customer: offered a one-time credit pending Lucy's review and documented mitigation steps. Customer extremely appreciative. :thumbsup:

mike_eng: Notes for follow-up: add a streaming detection on our side that emits a diagnostic header `X-Redwood-Stream-Diag: 1` in logs when streams end prematurely, and surface to support UI.

deploy-bot: Incident note saved to ops/incidents/1799994000-streaming-gateway-escalation (automated).
